sentences.text: The species name robustipes refers to the animal's strongly built feet.
Eurofluvioviridavis had a wide, flattened beak similar to that of modern tyrant flycatchers.
Its ulna was longer than the humerus and possessed eight to thirteen quill knobs where feathers attached.
The tarsometatarsus and feet of Eurofluvioviridavis resemble those of the genera Avolatavis and Vastanavis.
The semi-zygodactyl foot arrangement and raptor-like claws suggest Eurofluvioviridavis could grasp with its feet.
The holotype fossil SMNK.PAL.3835 was discovered in the lower middle Eocene Messel Pit near Darmstadt, Germany.
Eurofluvioviridavis is related to Avolatavis and Vastanavis within the family Vastanavidae.
Cladistic analyses support placing Vastanavis, Avolatavis, and Eurofluvioviridavis in the family Vastanavidae.
Eurofluvioviridavis lived in the Middle Eocene at the Messel Pit in Germany.
Eurofluvioviridavis lived between 48.07 and 41.03 million years ago during the Lutetian stage.
It is debated whether vastanavids are stem-group relatives of parrots or part of the stem group of Psittacopasseres.
It is possible that Avolatavis is a junior synonym of Eurofluvioviridavis, though this cannot yet be confirmed.
